messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: autoscaler-ceiling hit for gpu-pool-usw2. pool_max=120, pending_pods=82, queue_length=11,900, token-processing latencies rising. kpi: p95=1.8s -> 3.6s. Incident URL: https://internal.incidents/2210000000

sre-anna: ack. I'm attaching metrics and checking pending pod reasons. tagging infra and cloud-ops.

infra-mike: looking now. Initial check: cluster-autoscaler reports 'max nodes reached'. Also seeing a handful of pending pods with scheduling issues (taints/affinity).

eng-ben: confirmed backlog on model-serving (replicas scaled to desired but nodes can't land). This is causing request queueing and token throttling. Non-urgent batch jobs are running in the same pool too.

infra-mike: paste:```
kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-usw2 -o wide
# 120 nodes (all Ready)
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending | wc -l
82
kubectl describe pod inference/model-serve-abc-xyz | sed -n '1,120p'
# Events: 0/2 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 2 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeSelector.
```

cloud-ops-lee: quota check: GCP project has compute CPUs quota 150 (used 120), GPUs quota (nvidia-t4) limit 140 (used 120). We have headroom for +20 nodes but need to confirm regional GPU inventory.

support-jessica: customer-impact: A subset of hosted customers are seeing 502s and increased tail latency. Top affected tenants: acme-inc, quickchat, docs.ai. SLO alerting: error budget burn for hosted tier SLO-API is trending upward. I have an ongoing paging to AEs for impacted customers.

sre-anna: quick triage: cause = autoscaler policy hit manual ceiling (pool_max=120) + co-located batch jobs consuming GPUs. Options: (A) manual pool_max bump to 160 (temporary), (B) drain/migrate batch jobs out of gpu-pool, (C) evict lower-priority pods, (D) failover some traffic to cheaper model variants in other regions.

eng-ben: (D) will require routing changes and will take >15m. (B)/(C) doable faster but need careful eviction to avoid losing work. We should prefer immediate capacity increase to reduce customer impact while we clean up batch jobs.

oncall-next-tom: I'm oncall-next, can approve a one-time manual cap raise if cloud-ops confirms quota and infra coordinates the apply. Conditions: 1) set a timer to rollback after 30m if not needed, 2) avoid autoscaler thrash by setting a conservative scale-up rate, 3) notify billing.

cloud-ops-lee: confirmed: we can allocate +30 nodes in region (GPUs available), project quota allows it; watch for global region cross-constraints.

infra-mike: I'll run the manual override via terraform apply to bump pool_max to 150 and update autoscaler config (maxSurge/scaleDownDelay). Commands:```
# terraform workspace production
terraform plan -var 'gpu_pool_max=150' -out=plan.tfout
terraform apply plan.tfout
# then patch deployment to lower priority for batch jobs
kubectl label ns batch batch=low-priority --overwrite
```

deploy-bot: deploy started by infra-mike at 2026-03-15T02:24:30Z. CI checks passed.

infra-mike: manual cap bump applied. pool_max now 150. cluster-autoscaler logs: 'Nodes provisioning requested: 20'

incident-bot: update: autoscaler-ceiling -> overridden (manual). New nodes onboarding; pending_pods dropping from 82 -> 26 in next 90s.

eng-ben: traffic returning to normal for most requests. We'll keep lower-priority batch traffic evicted to ensure spare capacity. Can we set autoscaler to prefer serving pods? Suggest updating podPriority for model-serving to system-critical-equivalent.

support-jessica: sending customer comms: "We're seeing improvements after a capacity bump; mitigation is in progress; we'll follow up with RCA."

oncall-next-tom: handing off to oncall for next shift: please monitor for next 2 hours, watch cost and queue_length, and roll back pool_max to 120 when backlog cleared. I left a todo in the runbook.

cloud-ops-lee: scheduled automated rollback check at +30m: script will evaluate pending_pods and queue_length; if <=5% of baseline, it will restore pool_max to 120. Manual override remains possible.

sre-anna: incident severity -> Sev2 (multiple customers impacted but mitigation applied). Creating incident timeline and war-room notes. Action items: 1) RCA: why batch jobs were in gpu pool? 2) add quota / capacity playbook for manual raises, 3) improve autoscaler policy to auto-burst with safety guardrails.

infra-mike: done with initial cleanup, monitoring node join logs:```
# kubelet logs snippet
Mar 15 02:26:12 kubelet[...]: Node has joined cluster, kubernetes node ready
```

incident-bot: note: please add reactions to indicate ack: :thumbsup: for done items, :eyes: for watching.

support-jessica: marking affected customers and sending follow-up at T+1h.

oncall-next-tom: logging handoff: next oncall (sre-anna) will follow through. If any further throttling, escalate to infra+cloud-ops and re-open pager.

sre-anna: thanks. I'll own the postmortem and link to follow-up tasks. Closing live mitigation thread — continuing monitoring in #incidents and #eng-runtime.
